newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish citrus production hit by February frost.
newsitem.headline: Turkish citrus production hit by February frost.

text.p: A significant amount of Turkey's citrus production was affected by a frost that hit the country's southern regions in early February, officials said on Wednesday.
In Adana province about 17,500 hectares of citrus orchards were frozen, said Nihat Acar, provincial agricultural director in Adana, the top citrus-growing region in Turkey.
"The orchards damaged were about 90 percent of Adana region's total citrus capacity," he told Reuters.
He said frost also struck some wheat fields and greenhouses in the province but losses were negligible.
Temperatures on February 3-5 were around minus 10 Celsius -- seven degrees lower than normal temperatures for the region.
Similar reports came from the neighbouring Mersin region.
Ahmet Akinci, provincial agriculture director in Mersin, said a full assessment of the total damage in the southern provinces would be completed this week.
"The full information on the overall damage cannot be known until the final report comes out, which we expect this week," he said.
"The government has promised to compensate for farmers' losses, which amount to 6.5 trillion lira, by deferring their credit debts for one year."
Most of the losses in the Mersin area were from lemon trees, he said. Frost hit 3,300 hectares of citrus and 6,500 hectares of wheat.
Turkey annually produces about 25,000 tonnes of citrus fruit, about half of that oranges.
